transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-07
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 min
Attendees: Jamie Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Sofia Alvarez (Redwood PM); Maya Gonzales (Aurora PM), Liam O'Reilly (Aurora SA), Priya Nair (Aurora Ops), Derek Huang (Aurora Security)

Summary: technical sync to align on marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture for joint solution (Redwood hosted + Aurora marketplace), integration points for billing/entitlement, KMS/SSO considerations, and next steps for a small pilot listing.

[00:00] Jamie Chen: Okay hi everyone thanks for joining, good to see you all. quick roll call - we got raven? sorry Ravi are you on?
[00:08] Ravi Patel: yeah, hey everyone. I'm Ravi, I'm the solutions engineer on the Redwood side, mostly focused on runtime and integration points for marketplace deployments.
[00:15] Maya Gonzales: Maya here from Aurora, partner PM - thanks for setting this up, we want to make sure the listing process and the joint reference arch are smooth.
[00:22] Liam O'Reilly: Liam - solutions architect - we'll be owning the staging env and validating the integration.
[00:26] Derek Huang: Derek, security. I'll have a couple quick Qs around KMS and logs.
[00:30] Jamie Chen: Great. agenda - marketplace listing checklist, reference architecture draft, entitlements/billing integration, security/compliance checklist, and then action items. sound good?
[00:38] Priya Nair: Yep good.

[02:10] Ravi Patel: I'll kick off with a high-level of how Redwood shows up in a marketplace listing. There are two patterns we typically see: 1) Hosted listing where Redwood remains the control plane and the customer subscribes via marketplace and we provision a tenant on our hosted API; 2) Private/Bring-Your-Own Infra pattern where the listing points to a packaged deployable (cloud marketplace product that orchestrates a private deployment in the partner's cloud) - both are supported but the integration steps differ.
[02:45] Liam O'Reilly: For Aurora, we prefer the marketplace to support both but our initial goal is to get a hosted listing live so customers can consume quickly. Is there anything blocking from a technical perspective?
[02:55] Ravi Patel: No blockers, mostly documentation and a couple of artifacts: sample pricing metadata, a reference architecture diagram for the listing page, onboarding playbook, and a small smoke test we can run once we have a staging entitlement.
[03:10] Jamie Chen: we also provide a verified performance blurb for the listing - e.g., typical latency for 1k token generative workloads on our hosted plan. we'll share the benchmark results. note: those numbers vary by model, sequence length, quantization.
[03:30] Maya Gonzales: great - on the Aurora side we need a validated set of IAM roles and a manifest for the marketplace. Priya will own the manifest ingestion.

[05:00] [05:00] Liam O'Reilly: quick question on entitlements - when a customer purchases via Aurora marketplace, how does Redwood receive that entitlement? is it via a webhook, or do we poll a partner API?
[05:10] Ravi Patel: Good q. We support webhook-based entitlement callbacks - partner's marketplace sends an activation webhook that contains purchaser metadata and an entitlement token. alternatively we can support a polling integration to the marketplace's entitlement API. webhook is preferred for immediate provisioning.
[05:30] Jamie Chen: important to confirm how trial credits flow too - we'll need a mapping between Aurora SKU and Redwood trial bucket.
[05:40] Priya Nair: Aurora marketplace supports both trial SKUs and direct purchases; we'll provide a SKU mapping doc.

[07:20] Derek Huang: on security - KMS integration and tenant data isolation. question: if Redwood hosts customer workloads, who manages the encryption keys?
[07:30] Ravi Patel: by default Redwood manages keys for hosted listings (we KMS our data-in-transit and at-rest). For enterprise customers and some marketplace flows we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM - this is our recommended approach for regulated workloads. We'll need to confirm whether Aurora marketplace allows passing a customer KMS ARN during provisioning - that determines automation complexity.
[08:00] Derek Huang: yes we can pass an ARN in the provisioning payload, but we need a documented handshake for key usage and rotation.
[08:10] Jamie Chen: noted - Ravi will draft the KMS handshake and example policy.

[09:30] Ravi Patel: Reference architecture - I'll share my screen... (screen share noise) so here is the typical flow: marketplace -> entitlement webhook -> Redwood control plane -> token issuance -> provisioned tenant on Redwood hosted runtime -> usage metering -> billing events -> (optionally) callouts to customer's KMS or VPC peering for private deployments. In the hosted listing flow we also support network egress restrictions and regional routing to meet data residency.
[10:15] Maya Gonzales: couple clarifications: 1) For listings we need an architecture diagram that doesn't leak internal vendors' IPs, so use generic components; 2) we need a one-page integration checklist for our onboarding team.
[10:30] Jamie Chen: we can produce both - Ravi will do the diagram and Sofia will produce the one-pager.

[12:45] [12:45] Liam O'Reilly: what about webhook security - how do you sign or verify callbacks? we need to ensure Aurora can validate provisioning requests are legitimate.
[12:55] Ravi Patel: we sign webhooks with HMAC SHA256 and include a timestamp header. We also support mutual TLS for more sensitive partners. We can provide the verification code snippet for typical languages.
[13:10] Derek Huang: mTLS would be preferred for the enterprise flows. can you support cert rotation without downtime?
[13:20] Ravi Patel: yes, we have a dual-cert acceptance window for rotation - tested in our dedicated customers. we'll include that in the security doc.

[15:00] Priya Nair: For the listing metadata - we need: product title, short description, long description, sample API response, pricing tiers, support SLA, links to docs, logo assets (SVG + PNG), and a reference arch diagram. Anything else?
[15:20] Sofia Alvarez: include a sample eval harness (small prompt set) we used for the benchmark - helps customers validate quality on Aurora.
[15:30] Maya Gonzales: good call. also need contact for go-to-market ops and joint marketing permission.

[17:10] [17:10] Ravi Patel: On the subject of packaging for the private deploy option - Aurora supports a marketplace AMI/container bundle that triggers an automated private deploy. Redwood's private deployment package includes: Helm chart + infra scripts, post-install hook to register with the control plane, and an optional bootstrap script that configures KMS and SSO. We recently added an IaC module for Aurora-style networking that handles VPC endpoints and NVPC peering.
[17:50] Liam O'Reilly: that sounds good. For private listings we will run a validation test that instantiates the bundle in a sandbox account. what's the expected time-to-provision?
[18:00] Ravi Patel: currently approx 20-35 minutes for a minimal cluster + runtime; larger configs or data seeding can take longer. We'll provide a sizing table.

[19:40] Derek Huang: compliance - SOC2 scope and audit logs; we need to confirm log retention and whether Redwood can ship audit logs to our SIEM or to an S3 bucket.
[19:50] Jamie Chen: Redwood can push audit logs to a partner-managed S3 or support a push to a syslog endpoint; we have 90-day default retention on hosted but can extend per contract. For enterprise/private we can set retention and forward logs to customer SIEM.
[20:15] Derek Huang: perfect. also need cert for ISO/SOC scopes - you mentioned SOC2 earlier?
[20:20] Sofia Alvarez: yes Redwood is SOC2 Type II certified; we'll attach the cert and the security questionnaire.

[22:05] [22:05] Maya Gonzales: quick note on billing integration - Aurora wants to surface usage-based billing for the Redwood hosted plan. we need metering events and reconciliation reports. what's the cadence?
[22:20] Ravi Patel: we emit metering events in near realtime and produce daily usage reports via the partner API. For reconciliations we can produce CSVs and a summarized invoice feed. We also support exporting per-customer token usage.
[22:40] Priya Nair: can you produce a sandbox metering stream so we can verify ingestion?
[22:45] Ravi Patel: yes, we'll stand up a demo webhooks stream and a sample S3 export.

[24:30] Liam O'Reilly: about network connectivity - for private deployments customers will want VPC peering and private endpoints. do you support AWS endpoint services or require NAT?
[24:40] Ravi Patel: we support Endpoint Services (AWS PrivateLink) and VPC peering; we can also bind to an internal ELB. in our reference arch we'll indicate recommended pattern per deployment size.

[26:00] [26:00] Jamie Chen: Okay let's surface a tentative timeline: this week (7/7) alignment; by 7/12 Redwood shares checklist and PRD; by 7/14 Aurora provides staging account + manifest; by 7/16 Redwood provides reference arch + KMS handshake; week of 7/20 smoke test and demo - does that work?
[26:20] Maya Gonzales: yes that works for our PD.

[28:10] Ravi Patel: small gotcha we should call out - model compatibility. Redwood serves multiple model variants and quantization profiles; if Aurora marketplace wants a deterministic performance statement we should list a supported model set and a recommended default config for the listing. Otherwise customers may see variability.
[28:35] Maya Gonzales: understood. include a note in the listing that performance and latency vary by model and sequence length.

[30:00] [30:00] Derek Huang: one more security point - how do you handle PII deletion requests from a marketplace customer?
[30:10] Sofia Alvarez: We have data deletion APIs tied to tenant lifecycle; when a customer requests deletion we can enqueue a deletion job and provide confirmation. for hosted customers we also support data residency wipe within 48 hours for high-priority contracts.
[30:30] Derek Huang: ok we'll want those SLAs documented.

[32:15] Priya Nair: operational question - support handoff: who do Aurora customers contact if they have runtime issues after acquisition via our marketplace? do they call Redwood support directly or go through Aurora first?
[32:25] Jamie Chen: we typically do a joint-support model: marketplace purchase gets Aurora billing but Redwood provides first-line technical support via our partner support queue. We'll publish an escalation matrix and an SLA endpoint.
[32:45] Priya Nair: fine, we'll add that to the marketplace terms.

[35:00] [35:00] Liam O'Reilly: let's talk about the listing certification process - Aurora requires a sandbox acceptance test that runs three scenarios: provisioning, simple inference call, and entitlement revocation. Do you have an automated smoke test we can point at?
[35:15] Ravi Patel: yes, we have a smoke test harness (python + curl) that can run the three scenarios and emit pass/fail; we'll provide the repo link and a quickstart.
[35:30] Maya Gonzales: perfect. send the repo link and we can run it against our sandbox.

[37:40] [37:40] Jamie Chen: Any concerns about commercial terms? we touched on pricing mapping earlier - we'll send a sample price matrix and suggested revenue split options for marketplace resale.
[37:50] Priya Nair: we'll review but the ops team prefers per-seat + per-usage SKU. we'll take sample and feed back.

[40:00] Ravi Patel: small note: for private/bundled deployments we recommend enabling KV cache warmup in the bootstrap to reduce cold-start latency for initial requests. That is documented in the helm chart.
[40:20] Liam O'Reilly: good tip. we'll include that in validation.

[42:10] [42:10] Derek Huang: another item: auditability for rollbacks - if a tenant is deprovisioned, we need an auditable event with user id and justification. does your control plane record that?
[42:20] Ravi Patel: yes audit logs include user id, request payload, and we retain a chained log for 90 days (extendable). We'll include the log schema in the docs.

[44:30] Maya Gonzales: ok i think we're in good shape - final ask: can you bundle a sample listing page copy and suggested screenshots so we can expedite the QA for the marketplace UI?
[44:40] Sofia Alvarez: yes, we'll prepare a marketing-friendly short copy and a set of screenshots from the console and the performance blurb.

[46:00] [46:00] Jamie Chen: quick recap of action items: Jamie sends partner docs and listing checklist; Ravi drafts reference arch and KMS handshake; Sofia prepares one-page onboarding + listing copy; Maya will share Aurora manifest and sandbox creds; Derek will send compliance questions. schedule follow-up for week of 7/20 for a smoke test.
[46:25] Maya Gonzales: yep that's correct.

[48:00] [48:00] (brief crosstalk)
[48:10] Liam O'Reilly: small nit - when you share the reference arch can you include the terraform example for IAM roles? that will speed our infra folks.
[48:20] Ravi Patel: yes i'll include a minimal terraform snippet and example policies.

[50:30] Jamie Chen: alright thanks everyone - we'll follow up with the docs and link in an email. look forward to the smoke test.
[50:40] Maya Gonzales: thanks everyone bye.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription quality: medium - a few speaker attribution errors and minor word swaps (e.g., NVPC vs VPC in earlier notes).
